guideTitle: The Best Office Chairs for Shorter People
breadcrumbLabel: Best Office Chairs for Short People
metaTitle: Best Office Chairs for Short People: Low Seat Heights (2026)
metaDescription: We compared office chairs for shorter people on minimum seat height, seat depth, lumbar position and armrests, from budget mesh chairs to a petite-specific design.
introParagraphs: For shorter people, the chair's lowest setting matters more than its highest. If the seat can't drop far enough for your feet to rest flat, you end up perched on the front edge, away from the backrest and its lumbar support.

Seat depth is the second problem. A seat pan sized for an average adult can press behind the knees of a shorter sitter, which pushes you forward again. Adjustable seat depth, or a seat that is simply shallower, addresses it.

The eight chairs below all reach 16.5 inches or lower at their minimum, and range from under $40 to about $350 at the time of writing. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

bestoffice-budget-short.summary: A 15.7-inch minimum seat height, a 17.3-inch-wide seat and a mesh back for under $40.
bestoffice-budget-short.description:
The BestOffice is the lowest-cost way here to get a seat that drops to 15.7 inches, with a compact 17.3-inch-wide seat and a mesh back.

That low minimum is the key feature for shorter users, and the stated 250 lb capacity and adjustable armrests cover the basics. Lumbar support comes from a cushion, which you can at least reposition by hand.

Adjustment is limited beyond height, and the build is basic. For seat-depth adjustment, the SIHOO B100 is the step up.
bestoffice-budget-short.bestFor: Shorter people on a tight budget who mainly need a seat that goes low enough.
bestoffice-budget-short.skipIf: The seat is too deep for you on current chairs; the SIHOO B100's seat-depth adjustment addresses that.

neo-chair-certified-short.summary: A 15.5-inch minimum seat and BIFMA certification listed, at a budget price.
neo-chair-certified-short.description:
The NEO CHAIR goes slightly lower than the BestOffice, to 15.5 inches, and lists BIFMA certification, an industry standard for office furniture that few chairs at this price mention.

It has a mesh back, lumbar support, adjustable armrests and tilt. Its 18.9-inch maximum is low, which suits shorter users but limits who else can share it.

Padding is minimal and lumbar adjustment is limited.
cons: Low maximum height if the chair is shared
neo-chair-certified-short.bestFor: Shorter people who want a very low-cost chair with a listed industry certification.
neo-chair-certified-short.skipIf: You want adjustable lumbar; the HeroSet or Brick Attic offers it for a little more.

heroset-leather-short.summary: A PU leather high-back chair that drops to 14.6 inches, with adjustable lumbar.
heroset-leather-short.description:
The HeroSet suits shorter people who want a leather-style executive look: it combines PU leather and a high backrest with a 14.6-inch minimum seat height, one of the two lowest here.

It adds adjustable lumbar, 2D armrests and a stated 250 lb capacity at a moderate price. Adjustable lumbar matters for shorter torsos, since fixed lumbar is positioned for an average back.

PU leather holds more heat than mesh, and the listing doesn't mention seat-depth adjustment.
pros: Leather-style look at a moderate price
cons: PU leather is warmer than mesh
heroset-leather-short.bestFor: Shorter people who want a professional leather look and a very low seat.
heroset-leather-short.skipIf: You run warm; the Brick Attic offers a mesh back and lumbar at the same price.

brick-attic-short.summary: A compact seat depth, adjustable lumbar and a headrest for about $100.
brick-attic-short.description:
The Brick Attic is built around the seat-depth problem: its listing describes a compact seat depth intended to keep the front edge from pressing behind shorter users' knees.

It pairs that with a 15-inch minimum seat height, adjustable lumbar, a headrest and a mesh back at a moderate price, which makes it a well-rounded option if you can't adjust seat depth on your current chair.

The arms are 2D flip-up, so they fold away but offer limited adjustment. The listing gives no depth measurement, so compare its dimensions with your thigh length if you can.
pros: Compact seat depth for shorter legs
Mesh back at a moderate price
brick-attic-short.bestFor: Shorter people whose knees press against the front edge of standard seats.
brick-attic-short.skipIf: You want adjustable rather than fixed compact depth; the SIHOO B100 lets you set it.

gtplayer-gaming-short.summary: A gaming-style chair with a 15.5-inch minimum, recline and a 300 lb rating.
gtplayer-gaming-short.description:
The GTPLAYER is for shorter people who prefer a gaming-style chair: it reaches 15.5 inches, reclines, and comes with lumbar and headrest pillows.

It also carries a stated 300 lb capacity, higher than most chairs here, and adjustable armrests. The pillows can be repositioned by hand, which helps when a fixed lumbar sits too high for a shorter back.

The PU leather gaming look won't suit every room, and it holds more heat than mesh. Seat depth isn't listed.
cons: Gaming look won't suit every room
gtplayer-gaming-short.bestFor: Shorter people who want a reclining gaming-style chair with a low seat.
gtplayer-gaming-short.skipIf: You want a quieter office look; the Brick Attic or SIHOO B100 is the better fit.

comhoma-swing-short.summary: A 15.4-inch minimum seat with a swing mode for gentle rocking.
comhoma-swing-short.description:
The COMHOMA's distinguishing feature is a swing mode that lets the chair rock gently, which COMHOMA presents as a way to move while you work.

For shorter users, it also reaches 15.4 inches, has a mesh back, a lumbar cushion and adjustable armrests, and lists a 250 lb capacity at a low price.

Whether you want a chair that rocks is personal, and it may not suit a shared or quiet space. Lumbar support is a cushion rather than adjustable.
comhoma-swing-short.bestFor: Shorter people who like to move in their chair and want to stay on a small budget.
comhoma-swing-short.skipIf: You prefer a stable seat; the Brick Attic costs a little more and adds adjustable lumbar.

sihoo-b100-short.summary: Adjustable seat depth, adjustable lumbar, a headrest and a three-year warranty.
sihoo-b100-short.description:
The SIHOO B100 addresses the seat-depth problem directly: its seat depth adjusts, so you can shorten it until the front edge clears the back of your knees with your back against the lumbar.

It adds adjustable lumbar, a headrest, a mesh back and a stated three-year warranty at a mid-range price, which makes it the most complete ergonomic option here short of the TopJob Mochi.

Its 16.5-inch minimum is the highest in this guide. For the shortest users, or at a desk above standard height, that may still be too high without a footrest.
cons: Costs more than the budget picks
May need a footrest for the shortest users
sihoo-b100-short.bestFor: Shorter people whose main issue is seat depth rather than seat height.
sihoo-b100-short.skipIf: You need the lowest possible seat; the TopJob Mochi or HeroSet goes lower.

topjob-mochi-petite.summary: A chair sized for petite users, with a 14.5-inch minimum, 3D arms and a five-year warranty.
topjob-mochi-petite.description:
The TopJob Mochi is the only chair here designed specifically for petite users rather than adapted from a standard size: TopJob sizes the seat depth, seat width and backrest height for smaller frames.

It also has the lowest minimum seat height in this guide, 14.5 inches, plus adjustable lumbar, 3D armrests and a five-year warranty, the longest here.

It is the most expensive chair in the guide, and its smaller dimensions are unlikely to suit a household where people of different sizes share one chair.
specs: Seat and back: sized for petite users
pros: Seat and backrest sized for petite frames
cons: Most expensive chair in this guide
topjob-mochi-petite.bestFor: Petite users who want a chair sized for them throughout, not just a low seat.
topjob-mochi-petite.skipIf: The chair will be shared with taller people; the SIHOO B100's adjustable depth is more flexible.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Start with the minimum seat height
buyingCriteria.explanation: A common guideline is to sit with your feet flat on the floor, thighs roughly level and elbows near desk height. Compare the chair's minimum seat height with your own seated height, measured from the floor to the back of your knee with your feet flat. In this guide, minimums range from 14.5 inches (TopJob Mochi) to 16.5 inches (SIHOO B100).

If the seat is too deep, the front edge presses behind your knees and pushes you forward, away from the backrest. The SIHOO B100 has adjustable seat depth, the TopJob Mochi is sized for petite users, and the Brick Attic describes a compact seat.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Look for lumbar you can move
buyingCriteria.explanation: Fixed lumbar is positioned for an average torso and may sit too high on a shorter back. Adjustable lumbar, or a movable cushion or pillow, lets you place support where you need it.

If your desk is taller than about 29 to 30 inches, you may need to raise the chair to reach it, which lifts your feet. In that case a footrest, or a keyboard tray that lowers the work surface, can help.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Think about who else uses the chair
buyingCriteria.explanation: Chairs with low maximum heights, or petite-specific sizing, suit one shorter user well but may not work for taller people in the same household.

faq.q: What seat height do I need?
faq.a: It depends on your leg length and desk, not height alone. Sit with your feet flat and measure from the floor to the back of your knee; a chair whose minimum is at or below that figure should let your feet rest flat.

faq.q: Do I need a footrest if I'm short?
faq.a: If your chair can't go low enough, or you raise it to reach a tall desk, a footrest supports your feet at the right height. It is a practical fix when the chair and desk can't both fit you.

faq.q: Why doesn't my chair's lumbar support reach my lower back?
faq.a: Fixed lumbar is positioned for an average torso, so on a shorter back it may sit too high. A chair with adjustable lumbar, or a separate lumbar cushion you can place yourself, solves this.

faq.q: Can a shorter person use a standing desk comfortably?
faq.a: Yes, if the desk's minimum height is low enough for sitting and its range suits you when standing. Check the desk's minimum height before buying.

bottomLine: Start with the problem you actually have. If your feet don't reach the floor, the TopJob Mochi and HeroSet go lowest; if the seat is too deep, the SIHOO B100's adjustable depth is the most direct fix.

The Brick Attic is a well-rounded middle option with a compact seat, adjustable lumbar and a headrest, while the BestOffice and NEO CHAIR cover the basics on a small budget. The Mochi is the choice if you want a chair sized for petite users throughout.
